messages:
joel: Heads up — new devs hitting the quickstart are seeing sustained 429s when running the bulk-embeds demo with the default settings. Repro in a fresh org in <10s> :

anya: Which quickstart? python or node?

joel: Node quickstart. It launches 20 concurrent page fetches by default (parallelPages). That plus small token buckets on new orgs = instant throttle.

kevin: Oof. Is the client honoring Retry-After or does the paginator retry eagerly?

joel: It retries eagerly. Code just requeues pages without respecting Retry-After. snippet: ```js
// naive retry
await fetchPage().catch(()=>queue.push(page))
```

anya: Two small fixes we can ship fast: reduce default parallelPages to 3 and make paginator pause for the Retry-After duration + jitter. That avoids churn while keeping throughput reasonable.

kevin: Agree. Also want to flag SDK parity: Python SDK already exposes per-route rateLimit config but Node only has global concurrency. New users mix embed+gen calls and stomp on shared quota.

joel: Filed a tiny issue for node parity (link: https://git.redwood/rdw/rdw-sdk-node/issues/412). Proposed API: `client.rateLimit({route:'/v1/embeds', maxInFlight:4, windowMs:1000})`. Thoughts?

anya: That looks fine. We should also add an onboarding note in quickstart: "If you see 429s, reduce parallelism or wait for bucket refill." Short and front-loaded.

kevin: One more thought: client-side token bucket smoothing — keep a local estimate of tokens/sec per org and throttle to that when available. Cheap heuristic: on first few 429s, reduce concurrency by half and linearly ramp up.

joel: Love the heuristic. We'll add as an option in the Paginator: `smoothing: {enabled:true, initConcurrency:2, rampStep:1, backoffOn429:true}`.

ops-bot: incident-note: sampleapp quickstart generated 27 support tickets this week about "rate limit".

anya: Can we also teach the quickstart to read Retry-After headers? Some servers return seconds, others return HTTP-date. Implement a small parser.

kevin: Yep parse both formats and fallback to exponential backoff with cap if header missing/invalid. Pseudocode: ```
const t = parseRetryAfter(hdr) || (base * 2**attempt)
await sleep(t + randomJitter())
```

joel: I'll open the quick PR to: reduce default concurrency, add Retry-After pause, and wire smoothing toggle. Will tag @kevin for the SDK parity change and @anya for docs update.

anya: I'll add a 2-paragraph "client-side throttling patterns" blurb to docs/inference/rate-limits and link quickstart. Keep it short: per-route windows, respect Retry-After, smoothing.

kevin: After the change we should add an e2e that simulates intermittent 429 + Retry-After to prevent regressions. Also add a unit test for the Retry-After date parser.

joel: Sounds good. Plan: PR out today, CI run, then smoke test against a fresh demo org. If green we'll backport the change to the go/python samples as well. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: CI passed for branch fix/quickstart-burst (build #903) :white_check_mark:

anya: Nice. This should cut support noise a lot. Thanks for catching it, joel.

kevin: One follow-up item: product should consider an "onboarding burst buffer" in the hosted runtime so fresh orgs aren't immediately penalized. I'll file a product request.

joel: Filed product ticket (PRD-155). Marking this thread resolved after PR merges.

anya: closing loop — added a small note in quickstart README about reducing parallelism for small demo orgs.

kevin: closing: will follow up on SDK API this sprint."
